gold_answer: EfficientViT uses a lightweight multi-scale attention module that performs attention at multiple resolutions to capture both local and global features efficiently, replacing the computationally expensive standard multi-head self-attention.

EfficientViT: Multi-Scale Linear Attention for High-Resolution Dense Prediction

Figure 2: EfficientViT’s Building Block (left) and Multi-Scale Linear Attention (right). Left: EfficientViT’s building
block consists of a multi-scale linear attention module and an FFN with depthwise convolution (FFN+DWConv). Multi-
scale linear attention is responsible for capturing context information, while FFN+DWConv captures local information.
Right: After getting Q/K/V tokens via the linear projection layer, we generate multi-scale tokens by aggregating nearby
tokens via lightweight small-kernel convolutions. ReLU linear attention is applied to multi-scale tokens, and the outputs are
concatenated and fed to the final linear projection layer for feature fusing.

question: What computation reduction do MobileNets report for 3x3 depthwise separable convolutions versus standard convolutions?
gold_answer: Depthwise separable convolutions reduce computation by a factor of 1/N + 1/D_K^2 compared to standard convolutions, where N is the number of output channels and D_K is the kernel size. For a 3x3 kernel, this is 8-9x fewer computations.
answer: Extracted evidence: “MobileNet uses 3 × 3 depthwise separable convolutions which uses between 8 to 9 times less computation than stan- dard convolutions at only a small reduction in accuracy as seen in Section 4 . Additional factorization in spatial dimension such as in [ 16 , 31 ] does not save much additional computation as very little computation is spent in depthwise convolutions.” [P01, p.3, ev-P01-p3-t11-c0].

question: Compare the parameter efficiency of ViT-Base and EfficientNet-B7 on ImageNet classification.
gold_answer: ViT-Base/16 has about 86M parameters achieving ~77.9% ImageNet top-1 (when trained only on ImageNet), while EfficientNet-B7 has 66M parameters achieving 84.3% top-1, making EfficientNet-B7 more parameter efficient for ImageNet classification. However, ViT benefits more from large-scale pre-training.
answer:
Extracted evidence: “Table 2. EfficientNet Performance Results on ImageNet (Russakovsky et al., 2015). All EfficientNet models are scaled from our baseline EfficientNet-B0 using different compound coefficient φ in Equation 3. ConvNets with similar top-1/top-5 accuracy are grouped together for efficiency comparison. Our scaled EfficientNet models consistently reduce parameters and FLOPS by an order of magnitude (up to 8.4x parameter reduction and up to 16x FLOPS reduction) than existing ConvNets.” [P02, p.6, ev-P02-p6-cap1-c0].
Extracted evidence: “First, we pre-train ViT models on datasets of increasing size: ImageNet, ImageNet-21k, and JFT- 300M. To boost the performance on the smaller datasets, we optimize three basic regularization parameters – weight decay, dropout, and label smoothing. Figure 3 shows the results after fine- tuning to ImageNet (results on other datasets are shown in Table 5) 2 . When pre-trained on the smallest dataset, ImageNet, ViT-Large models underperform compared to ViT-Base models, despite (moderate) regularization. With ImageNet-21k pre-training, their performances are similar. Only with JFT-300M, do we see the full benefit of larger models. Figure 3 also shows the performance” [P03, p.6, ev-P03-p6-t26-c0].
